I'm Shixiao (Forainest) Wang 王仕虓, a PhD researcher at the University of Birmingham, working on neural decoding and co-embodied intelligence.

I study how brain and muscle signals can help robots interpret intended movements. My longer-term goal is to use these signals to control wearable devices that assist movement.

Current research

How can robots interpret
intended movements?

My current work focuses on neural and motion signals, with wearable assistance as a longer-term application.

Ongoing research

Symbiosis

Wearable robots that
work with the body.

Symbiosis is my ongoing research on co-embodied intelligence. I am exploring how a wearable system could use signals from the user and the environment to decide when and how to assist movement.

Contact me about Symbiosis ↗
Sense

Multimodal intent understanding

I am designing ways to align EEG, EMG, gaze and motion recordings, and to assess when each signal is reliable enough to inform a decision.

Predict

Shared world models

I am exploring models that represent the user and robot together, and predict movement while accounting for intent and physical constraints.

Assist

Closed-loop augmentation

The next steps are to test assistance and feedback in simulation, then evaluate how the components work together in a closed loop.
